subjects.description: Vectors, matrices and the differential calculus the rest of the tree needs.
subjects.name: Linear Algebra & Calculus

skills.description: A function $f:X\to Y$ assigns each element of a domain $X$ a unique image in $Y$. Sets, tuples and indexed families are the vocabulary every later definition uses.
skills.name: Sets & Functions

skills.description: A vector $\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ is an ordered tuple; addition and scalar multiplication obey the vector-space axioms. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Vectors & Vector Spaces

skills.description: A matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ encodes a linear map $\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$; $(AB)_{ij}=\sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}$. Likelihood matrices $A$ in active inference are exactly this.
skills.name: Matrices & Matrix Multiplication

skills.description: The inner product $\langle\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\rangle=\sum_i x_i y_i$ underlies expectations $\mathbb{E}_p[f]=\langle p, f\rangle$ used everywhere below. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Inner Products & Norms

skills.description: For $A\mathbf{v}=\lambda\mathbf{v}$, $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue; covariance and precision matrices are symmetric positive-definite. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Eigenvalues & Positive-Definiteness

skills.description: Continuity formalises 'small input change → small output change', the precondition for differentiation. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Limits & Continuity

subjects.description: From gradient descent to functional derivatives. It groups concepts that learners reuse directly in later strata and in the SkillTree learning path.
subjects.name: Optimisation & Variational Calculus

skills.description: The gradient $\nabla f(\mathbf{x})$ stacks partial derivatives and points in the direction of steepest ascent — the engine of every optimisation below.
skills.name: Derivatives & Gradients

skills.description: $(f\circ g)'(x)=f'(g(x))\,g'(x)$; backpropagation and message passing are repeated chain-rule applications. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: The Chain Rule

skills.description: The Jacobian collects first partials of a vector field; the Hessian collects second partials and certifies local curvature/convexity.
skills.name: Jacobian & Hessian

skills.description: A convex function lies below its chords: $f(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\le \lambda f(x)+(1-\lambda)f(y)$. Convexity guarantees a unique minimum — and powers Jensen's inequality later.
skills.name: Convexity

skills.description: Gradient descent steps downhill; a fixed point $\nabla f=0$ is a stationary belief — perception in active inference is gradient descent on free energy.
skills.name: Gradient Descent & Fixed Points

skills.description: Normalisation $\sum_i q_i=1$ is an equality constraint; Lagrange multipliers yield the softmax as the maximum-entropy solution. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Constrained Optimisation & Lagrange Multipliers

skills.description: A functional maps a function to a scalar; the functional derivative $\delta F/\delta q$ minimises free energy over the whole density $q$, not a single point.
skills.name: Functionals & the Calculus of Variations

skills.description: Setting $\delta F/\delta q=0$ subject to normalisation gives the variational update; this is the mathematical skeleton of the Free Energy Principle.
skills.name: Euler–Lagrange & Stationarity

subjects.description: Axioms, random variables, Bayes' theorem and expectation. It groups concepts that learners reuse directly in later strata and in the SkillTree learning path.
subjects.name: Probability Foundations

skills.description: Probabilities are non-negative, the sure event has probability 1, and disjoint events add. Everything Bayesian rests on these three rules.
skills.name: Probability Axioms

skills.description: A random variable assigns numbers to outcomes; its distribution lists the probability of each value. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Random Variables

skills.description: Marginalisation $p(x)=\sum_y p(x,y)$ and conditioning $p(x\mid y)=p(x,y)/p(y)$ are the two moves of all inference. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Joint, Marginal & Conditional

skills.description: $X\perp Y$ iff $p(x,y)=p(x)p(y)$; independence makes mutual information zero. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Independence

skills.description: $p(s\mid o)=\dfrac{p(o\mid s)p(s)}{p(o)}$ — posterior $\propto$ likelihood $\times$ prior. This single identity is the seed of perception-as-inference. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Bayes' Theorem

skills.description: $\mathbb{E}_p[f]=\sum_x p(x)f(x)$ and $\mathrm{Var}=\mathbb{E}[(X-\mathbb{E}X)^2]$; free energy is an expectation under the recognition density. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Expectation & Variance

subjects.description: The distribution zoo and Markov dynamics. It groups concepts that learners reuse directly in later strata and in the SkillTree learning path.
subjects.name: Distributions & Stochastic Processes

skills.description: A Bernoulli$(\theta)$ models one coin flip; the binomial sums $n$ of them. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Bernoulli & Binomial

skills.description: A categorical distribution is a probability vector over $K$ states — the data type of beliefs $q(s)$ in discrete active inference.
skills.name: Categorical & Multinomial

skills.description: A Markov chain's next state depends only on the current state: $p(s_{t+1}\mid s_{1:t})=p(s_{t+1}\mid s_t)$. Transition matrices $B$ are exactly Markov kernels.

skills.description: A stationary distribution is invariant under the transition; the FEP characterises living systems by a non-equilibrium steady state.

subjects.description: Surprise, entropy, cross-entropy, KL and the key inequalities. It groups concepts that learners reuse directly in later strata and in the SkillTree learning path.
subjects.name: Entropy & Divergence

skills.description: Rare events are surprising: surprise $=-\ln p(o)$. A probability-$0.01$ event carries 4.60517 nats of surprise. Minimising expected surprise is the FEP in one line.
skills.name: Surprise (Self-Information)

skills.description: Entropy $H(p)=-\sum_x p(x)\ln p(x)$ is expected surprise. A fair coin has 0.693147 nats; a fair die has 1.79176 nats; a biased (0.9/0.1) coin only 0.325083 nats — certainty lowers entropy.
skills.name: Shannon Entropy

skills.description: $H(p,q)=-\sum_x p(x)\ln q(x)$ is the expected surprise of using $q$ when reality is $p$; it decomposes as $H(p)+\mathrm{KL}(p\|q)$.
skills.name: Cross-Entropy

skills.description: $\mathrm{KL}(p\|q)=\sum_x p(x)\ln\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\ge 0$, zero iff $p=q$ (Gibbs). A 0.9/0.1 coin diverges from fair by 0.368064 nats. KL is the 'complexity' term of free energy.
skills.name: Kullback–Leibler Divergence

skills.description: Gibbs' inequality $\mathrm{KL}(p\|q)\ge 0$ follows from the concavity of $\ln$; it guarantees free energy upper-bounds surprise. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Gibbs' Inequality

skills.description: For convex $\varphi$, $\varphi(\mathbb{E}[X])\le\mathbb{E}[\varphi(X)]$. Applied to $-\ln$, Jensen yields the evidence lower bound (ELBO). Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Jensen's Inequality

subjects.description: Shared information, Bayesian surprise and maximum entropy. It groups concepts that learners reuse directly in later strata and in the SkillTree learning path.
subjects.name: Mutual Information & Bounds

skills.description: $H(X,Y)$ and $H(Y\mid X)$ measure uncertainty of pairs and residual uncertainty; $H(X,Y)=H(X)+H(Y\mid X)$ (chain rule of entropy). Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.
skills.name: Joint & Conditional Entropy

skills.description: $I(X;Y)=\mathrm{KL}(p(x,y)\|p(x)p(y))\ge 0$, zero iff independent. A correlated 0.4/0.1/0.1/0.4 joint shares 0.192745 nats. Epistemic value is expected mutual information between states and observations.
skills.name: Mutual Information

skills.description: Bayesian surprise is $\mathrm{KL}(\text{posterior}\|\text{prior})$ — the information an observation provides. It is the epistemic drive of active inference.
skills.name: Information Gain & Bayesian Surprise

skills.description: $\sigma(\mathbf{x})_i=\frac{e^{\beta x_i}}{\sum_j e^{\beta x_j}}$ is the max-entropy distribution for given expected scores. With scores $[1,2,3]$ the top mass is 0.665241 at precision 1 and 0.95033 at precision 3 — precision sharpens choice.
skills.name: The Softmax / Gibbs Distribution

skills.description: Exact inference needs the evidence $p(o)=\sum_s p(o\mid s)p(s)$, which is exponential in the number of latent variables — motivating approximation.
skills.name: Exact Bayesian Inference & Intractability

skills.description: Active inference replaces the true posterior with a tractable recognition density $q(s)$ and improves it by minimising free energy.
skills.name: Recognition Density $q(s)$

skills.description: With a 1%-prevalence condition and a 99%-sensitive / 95%-specific test, a positive result yields posterior 0.166667 for the condition — base rates dominate.

subjects.description: The ELBO, free energy, mean-field, Laplace and message passing. It groups concepts that learners reuse directly in later strata and in the SkillTree learning path.

skills.description: Jensen gives $\ln p(o)\ge \mathbb{E}_q[\ln p(o,s)-\ln q(s)]=\text{ELBO}$. Maximising the ELBO is minimising variational free energy. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.

skills.description: $F=\mathrm{KL}(q\|\text{prior})-\mathbb{E}_q[\ln p(o\mid s)]=$ complexity $-$ accuracy $=$ surprise $+\,\mathrm{KL}(q\|\text{posterior})$. $F$ upper-bounds surprise and is tight when $q$ is the true posterior.
skills.name: Variational Free Energy

skills.description: On the noisy-sensor model, a uniform belief has $F=$3.11735 nats while the true posterior has $F=$2.82346 nats, exactly the negative log-evidence 2.82346 nats — the bound is tight.
skills.name: Tightness of the Free-Energy Bound

skills.description: Iterating $q\leftarrow q-\eta\,\delta F/\delta q$ drives $F$ from 3.11735 nats down to 2.82346 nats — perception is inference by free-energy descent.

skills.description: Assuming $q(s_1,\dots,s_n)=\prod_i q_i(s_i)$ decouples the variational updates into per-factor fixed-point equations. Learners should be able to state the concept, connect it to its prerequisites, and explain the downstream Active Inference move it makes possible.

skills.description: Expanding $\ln p$ to second order at the MAP gives a Gaussian $q$; continuous active inference uses the Laplace-encoded free energy.

skills.description: If person A holds a generative model $p_A(o,s)$ and person B holds $p_B(o,s)$, then conditioning on the same observation $o$ makes their posteriors $p_A(s\mid o)$ and $p_B(s\mid o)$ estimates of the same hidden cause. Communication couples the models further: one agent's posterior can act as another's prior, and an ecosystem-level observer can pool the individual posteriors into a population-level belief over $s$. How tightly the population converges depends on the precision each agent assigns its evidence and on the diversity of their priors, so it is this coupling — not any single mind — that the information-ecosystem view actually treats as one generative model.
skills.name: Coupling Generative Models Across Minds
